candidates.title: Canada's 'Railway City' wants passenger trains back. Like in much of the country, it's not so simple
candidates.description: Canada is spending billions to expand passenger rail after decades of decline, but torn-up tracks, lost corridors and a surviving network built around freight means communities trying to bring trains back face a very different railway than the one they lost.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A 14th B.C. Conservative MLA leaves caucus as calls grow for leader to resign
candidates.description: Linda Hepner, who serves in the Surrey-Serpentine River riding, told CBC News Sunday morning she has resigned from Conservative caucus "effective immediately."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Should municipalities ban smart glasses in pools and change rooms?
candidates.description: Some city councils are banning smart glasses in public change rooms to prevent people from being covertly recorded, but 10 Canadian municipalities contacted by CBC News say existing rules are sufficient.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: La Bola Negra headlines TIFF Awards with People's Choice nod
candidates.description: La Bola Negra, directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, is an epic that spans the interconnected lives of three gay men in Spain.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Long-standing Winnipeg hotel reconnects with 'piece of history' after nearly 120 years
candidates.description: The Northern Hotel on Winnipeg's Main Street has reconnected with a piece of its history, after an Alberta-based antiques dealer stumbled upon a custom cash register made for the business more than a century ago.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Agent Layla': Sex assault victim turned secret agent brings her abuser to justice
candidates.description: A new CBC Podcast tells how Vienna Luke, the victim of a historic sexual assault, went undercover as an RCMP agent to record a confession from the family member who assaulted her years earlier.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New Bluetooth tags let anyone track monarch butterfly migration in real time
candidates.description: For the first time, Nature NB deployed new Bluetooth-enabled tags on monarch butterflies in New Brunswick this year, allowing anyone with a smartphone to help track their journey to Mexico in real time.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: OSAP delay sends Ontario college students home on 1st day of school
candidates.description: Maya Tilley had planned her year around a new college program, but instead of walking into class on the first day, she found herself being sent home — along with about a dozen other students — because their OSAP funding had not arrived.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: From 'The World’s Greatest Lover' to 'The Happy Jogger': The people who walked across Canada before Terry Fox
candidates.description: Terry Fox may be the most famous person to attempt to cross Canada on foot, but he wasn’t the first, writes Ainsley Hawthorn.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: To get eyes on Canadian films, indie cinemas group calls for big studios to relax their grip
candidates.description: An industry group that represents independent cinemas across the country says its members already bring in the majority of box office revenue for Canadian films - but that they need help to get even more eyeballs on homegrown content.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The province gave SMU $25M to transform health care. Then it quietly killed the plan
candidates.description: The Nova Scotia government gave Saint Mary's University $25 million in 2023 to create health-care data analytics and management programs to revolutionize the province's health-care system. Less than three years after a high-profile announcement was made, the province quietly shut down the initiative.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New Brunswick is weaving AI into its K-12 curriculum, drawing praise — and pushback
candidates.description: New Brunswick is incorporating learning about AI into its anglophone K-12 curriculum, amid wider calls to emphasize teaching young Canadians how to responsibly use the technology for school. However, some are calling for a pause and pushing back, especially when it comes to the youngest learners.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ‘Holy moly!’: Rare shark visit to Nova Scotia's Bedford Basin inspires shock and awe
candidates.description: It’s been a long time since swimming was encouraged in the Bedford Basin, but that didn’t stop one shark from making a prolonged — and very rare — visit to the water on Friday night.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UCP riding group demands leadership review as separatist leader criticizes Danielle Smith's unity stance
candidates.description: To force a party vote on the premier's leadership, 22 riding associations would need to make same request.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 6 people injured after vehicle strikes pedestrians at festival in Saint-Tite, Que.
candidates.description: The incident happened on Saint-Joseph Boulevard in Saint-Tite, Que. on the site of the Festival Western de Saint-Tite, a major attraction for the region that is wrapping up this weekend. All six pedestrians are expected to survive.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The province is proposing a ‘working forest’ model — but what does that mean?
candidates.description: B.C. is testing out a new forestry model in Campbell River that it says will reduce industry red tape for the struggling sector. But advocates and experts have concerns over its "no-net-loss" approach.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ‘It’s a form of therapy’: Quebec line dancing school sees boom in attendance
candidates.description: A country line dancing school in Saint-Lazare, Que., has recently experienced an exponential increase in attendance. As a result, it’s had to add more classes, reaching 10 different locations in the greater Montreal area.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Family of Bhishma Rajyaguru, killed in crash with Sask. Roughrider, mourns his death
candidates.description: Bhishma Rajyaguru's father and sister remember him after he died when ​Saskatchewan Roughrider​ Jayden Dalke crashed into his vehicle.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian men's volleyball team falls to Cuba in Olympic qualifier final
candidates.description: Canada's men's volleyball team fell 3-1 to Cuba in the final of continental qualifications for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics on Saturday in Moncton, N.B.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Protection for women who defy the Mafia is changing in Italy. Does it go far enough?
candidates.description: For women speaking out against the Mafia, the protection offered can be both practically and emotionally challenging. A new Italian law extending protection from organized crime to children and the adults caring for them — often their mothers — is designed to address some of that gap.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Head of European Investment Bank eyes Canada opportunities as Carney pushes EU ties
candidates.description: The president of the European Union's investment bank says "the time is ripe" to deepen its co-operation with Canada by exploring how to finance Canadian projects — comments that come as Prime Minister Mark Carney pushes for more EU ties.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 18 suspects in 2021 assassination of Haiti leader to be extradited to U.S. to face trial
candidates.description: Eighteen suspects who were arrested in the July 2021 killing of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse were awaiting extradition to the U.S. on Sunday, marking the end of a drawn-out judicial process in Haiti for a killing that shocked the troubled Caribbean country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Germany's Merz vows to press on with reforms despite state election losses to far-right AfD
candidates.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz suffered a bruising electoral setback in two state elections on Sunday, including a historic defeat for his party, but vowed to press ahead with potentially painful reforms to Europe's biggest economy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why Prince Harry and Meghan face more challenges after their return to the U.K.
candidates.description: Issues that arose when Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, stepped back from official duties in 2020, along with new challenges around concerns such as security, are front and centre after their return to Britain.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ukraine fires more than 1,000 drones at Russia, including hundreds launched at Moscow
candidates.description: Across the wider Moscow region, the attack killed two people and wounded 20, local Gov. Andrei Vorobyov said. The dead were a 74-year-old man and a 44-year-old woman, he said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says proposed triumphal arch near White House would house drones, snipers
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Sunday the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian drones are stalking Ukrainian trains and trying to hobble the country's rail system
candidates.description: In recent weeks, Russia has stepped up drone strikes on Ukraine's rail network, targeting trains and the approximately 20,000 kilometres of track that form a key transportation artery across the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: North Korea fires two ballistic missiles off east coast in three hours
candidates.description: North Korea launched two missiles off its eastern coast on Sunday, its second set of tests in roughly a week and days after Pyongyang accused the U.S. of driving tensions on the Korean Peninsula through a series of military drills.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Saudi Arabia confirms Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack its capital with a ballistic missile
candidates.description: Saudi Arabia on Saturday confirmed that Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack its capital with a ballistic missile, the first targeting of Riyadh since the escalation in fighting with the Tehran-backed rebels that has opened a new front in the Iran war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico say journalists denied access to White House after Trump ban
candidates.description: Reporters from three major news organizations — CNN, MS NOW and Politico — were denied access to the White House on Saturday, a day after U.S. President Donald Trump said he was barring them because of reporting he found to be "fake news."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Greenland, Denmark say deal with U.S. will not cede sovereignty
candidates.description: Denmark and Greenland on Saturday said any agreement with the United States would not compromise Greenland's sovereignty, after President Donald Trump said the deal would give Washington "permanent control" over the Arctic island's security, leaving its precise scope unclear.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada won't pay directly into EU budget under Carney's plan: ambassador-designate
candidates.description: As Prime Minister Mark Carney presses toward creating a "unique alliance" with the European Union, Canada's ambassador is ruling out paying directly into the 27-nation bloc's budget.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israel moving ahead with settlement plans that would split West Bank in two, rights group says
candidates.description: Rights groups say the Israeli government is forging ahead with a contentious settlement expansion plan that would effectively divide the occupied West Bank, long criticized as a threat to the viability of a future Palestinian state.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says deal struck to boost U.S. military presence in Greenland
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland after months of threatening to take island by force from the NATO ally.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump announces White House ban on CNN, other media outlets
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an immediate White House ban on a number of news outlets, including CNN.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Former Pakistani PM Imran Khan’s son says he fears for his father's life behind bars
candidates.description: Kasim Khan, the the son of jailed former Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan, says he wakes up most mornings expecting to learn that his father has died in prison.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror breaks silence, says he didn't have 'any doubts' of her guilt
candidates.description: The lone juror who wanted to convict Lindsay Clancy of murder for killing her three children said he was certain of her guilt, but that other jurors wouldn’t listen to him, according to a statement released by his lawyer Friday in his first public comments on the case.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Is AI evolving too fast? A look at the debate on slowing it down
candidates.description: The path forward for artificial intelligence is caught between promises of breakthroughs that would benefit humanity and concerns the technology will grow too powerful for human good. Here's a look at which tech and world leaders are calling for a slowdown in AI's development.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Not just lemonade stands: How a new wave of 'kid-preneurs' are making their own money
candidates.description: Across Canada, kids are getting an early taste of entrepreneurship — earning money, testing their ideas and learning skills they can carry into adulthood. Experts say social media, AI and the rising cost of living may be helping fuel the trend.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. import ban on Canadian molasses highlights sticky sugar industry feud
candidates.description: The Trump administration's announcement of a ban on importing Canadian molasses left some scratching their heads. The ban, set to hit on Sept. 29, has resurfaced allegations of sugar smuggling and a battle between North American sugar giants.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ed Sheeran admits 'mistakes' at first show since Macklemore controversy
candidates.description: The singer spoke about Israel and Gaza after Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian remarks on stage.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex with drones and snipers
candidates.description: Trump said the updated plans were at the request of the US military and for national security purposes.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Houthis say they targeted Saudi capital with ballistic missiles
candidates.description: A reported strike on a fuel depot at Riyadh airport caused delays on Saturday, as Saudi Arabia says it shot down a ballistic missile aimed at the capital.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control'
candidates.description: Denmark and the US have reached an agreement after months of threats from Donald Trump to annex the territory.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
candidates.description: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa
candidates.description: Dineo Motapane is one of nine recent victims whose deaths have left a nation traumatised over the level of violence against women.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump says US will form 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar
candidates.description: The president said his administration "will not in any way hinder or stifle the growth" amid amid warnings about the emergent technology.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Shark attack prompts rare kill order in Western Australia as victim named
candidates.description: Greg O'Neill "loved the ocean", his family say, as police boats and helicopters patrol Perth's beaches in search of his body and the shark that attacked him.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Cultural treasures are being destroyed worldwide - so why is no-one being punished?
candidates.description: A cauldron of conflicts is bubbling across the world, with cultural monuments being destroyed. These people are fighting against it.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks
candidates.description: An embattled Trump has injected his fight with the news media with new acrimony, writes the BBC's Anthony Zurcher.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Mum's viral barefoot race sparks debate over India's education crisis
candidates.description: The 47-year-old ran - and won - a 3km race where she hoped to win enough prize money to buy study books for her daughter.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Not all AI workers think the tech could kill everyone
candidates.description: In text exchanges and conversations, multiple people who have worked for leading companies are sceptical of the warnings.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Tata Sons: India's corporate crown braces for upheaval amid boardroom revolt
candidates.description: The Tata boardroom battle has intensified over a re-appointment of its chairman and a diktat to go public.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Fans react as Ed Sheeran speaks out over Macklemore controversy at show
candidates.description: Ed Sheeran told the crowd he had made mistakes after Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian remarks.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Concertgoers and pro-Palestinian activists arrive at Ed Sheeran concert
candidates.description: Some Ed Sheeran fans say they are excited to enjoy music and are not there for politics after Macklemore was dropped from the tour for making pro-Palestinian comments.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Enough is enough': Women protest after string of murders near Johannesburg
candidates.description: The police have since set up a task team to investigate the murders and have urged women in the Kempton Park area to avoid walking or running alone "particularly in isolated areas".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Is the Kennedy Center losing 'hundreds of millions of dollars'?
candidates.description: Records in 2024 show the venue had a surplus of millions of dollars once contributions and grants had been factored in.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Would Australians support a smart glasses ban?
candidates.description: As Australia considers barring the use of smart glasses in government offices, the BBC asks people in Sydney what they think.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'You never quite know what you're going to pull out'
candidates.description: The group is marking a decade of fishing everything from an inflatable doll to a Nintendo out of the harbour.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: When did grey squirrels start posing a threat to reds?
candidates.description: A pair of grey squirrels was reportedly brought to the United Kingdom by a Cheshire banker in 1876.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Germany's Merz vows to press ahead with reforms after historic state election defeat
candidates.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has faced a major electoral setback in two state elections, with his center-right party losing ground. The far-right Alternative for Germany party made significant gains.

candidates.title: PHOTOS: The precarious life of fisherfolk
candidates.description: In the bustling heart of the southern Indian city of Chennai is a market that never sleeps, where residents from the poorest neighborhoods wage a battle of survival with the sea.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ukraine fires over 1,000 drones at Russia, including hundreds launched at Moscow
candidates.description: Moscow's mayor described the wave of drones as the "largest ever" attack on the Russian capital and said there had been damage to a Moscow oil refinery and a residential building.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Saudi Arabia says Houthis tried to attack its capital
candidates.description: Saudi Arabia said Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack Riyadh with a ballistic missile, the first time its capital has been targeted since the escalation in fighting with the Iran-backed rebels.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The new lines of southern Lebanon
candidates.description: The U.N. expanded the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon's mandate 20 years ago to include monitoring adherence to a ceasefire in fighting between Israel and Lebanon's Iran-backed Hezbollah — the militant group created in 1982 to counter a second Israeli invasion.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: France, Poland and European allies warn of escalating Russian 'hybrid' attacks
candidates.description: The leaders of France, Poland, and other leading European nations are alarmed over what they describe as Russian "hybrid" attacks.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Life in Kabul 5 years after the Taliban's return
candidates.description: Five years after the return of Taliban rule, NPR visited Kabul to see how Afghans are dealing with their new government's strict social restrictions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Russia holds parliamentary vote in areas it seized from Ukraine in the war
candidates.description: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread
candidates.description: Italian health authorities see evidence that rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across a wider area, during more months of the year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. and Denmark reach deal to build U.S. military presence in Greenland
candidates.description: President Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Judge orders Fox to hand over hundreds of documents in shareholders' case
candidates.description: Fox Corp. must turn over hundreds of documents that could shed light on how founder Rupert Murdoch handled some of his media companies' biggest scandals.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
candidates.description: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How a pizza app changed our relationship with waiting
candidates.description: Status trackers are ubiquitous on online apps and ordering. We have the story the seminal Domino's Pizza Tracker that led to many copies, and we check on why many of the trackers now aren't accurate.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
candidates.description: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
candidates.description: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Betel nuts are a top mind-affecting substance. Now there's evidence of ancient use
candidates.description: New research on ancient human remains suggests the habitual usage of betel nuts, a plant seed with mind-affecting properties that is popular in parts of Asia despite the health risks it presents.
candidates.author: NPR
